reason: The text contains instances where Hebrew leaders, particularly Moses, express frustration and complaints about the people. Most notably, when facing a water shortage at Rephidim, Moses cries out to God saying, 'What shall I do unto this people? for they are almost ready to stone me' (Exodus 17:4). Additionally, Moses repeatedly expresses exasperation with the people's complaints and lack of faith, as seen when he asks them 'Why do you quarrel with me? Why do you test the Lord?' when they murmur about lack of water. These represent the leaders complaining about the people's behavior, though the text shows more instances of people complaining to leaders than leaders complaining about people.
